chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, they said: We mentioned to him (peace be upon him) Kufa and the land tax levied upon it, and what the people of his household had acquired in it, so he said:

"Whoever voluntarily submits, his land is left in his hand, and the tenth (ushr) is taken from him for what is watered by rain and rivers, and half the tenth for what was rare in what they cultivated of it. And what they did not cultivate of it, the Imam takes and leases it to whoever cultivates it, and it belongs to the Muslims. And upon those who lease it, in their shares, is the tenth and half the tenth. And there is no zakat in less than five awsiq. And what is conquered by the sword, that is for the Imam to lease as he sees fit, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did with Khaybar; he leased its black land and its white land, meaning its land and its palm trees. And the people say that leasing the land and palm trees is not suitable, yet the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) leased Khaybar. And upon those who lease, besides the leasing of the land, is the tenth and half the tenth in their shares."

And he said: "Indeed, the people of Ta'if submitted, and the tenth and half the tenth were imposed upon them. And indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Mecca by conquest, and they were captives in his hand, he freed them and said: 'Go, you are free.'

And he said: "Indeed, the people of Ta'if submitted, and the tenth and half the tenth were imposed upon them. And indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Mecca by conquest, and they were captives in his hand, he freed them and said: 'Go, you are free.'

key_terms.الْأَوْسَاق: Plural of sa', a unit of volume/weight for zakat threshold
key_terms.خَيْبَرَ: Khaybar (a historical region known for its fertile land)

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic rules for land tax and agricultural tithe according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the jurisprudential distinction between voluntary submission (*islām*) and conquest by force (*futūḥ*), establishing that land tax (*kharāj*) and tithe (*ushr*) rates vary based on irrigation methods and the Imam's discretion. It reinforces the authority of the Imam to allocate conquered lands, citing the precedent of Khaybar, while also noting the emancipation of Mecca's inhabitants as a model of grace upon conquest. This text is crucial for understanding the Shia view on agricultural zakat thresholds and the flexibility of land distribution in governance.
